claim_summary: For prime \(p\ge5\) and \(1\le r<p\), the complete intersection of the degree-one, degree-two and degree-three power sums in \(p+r\) projective coordinates is normal, geometrically integral and has exactly \(\binom{p+r}{p}\) reduced ordinary-double-point singularities, all over \(\mathbb F_p\).
integrity: The arbitrary-prime theorem is proved by a Jacobian two-value classification and nondegenerate completed-local quadratic form. Finite checker is corroboration, not proof; no independent validation is asserted.
scientific_limitations: Only p>=5, p<n<2p, degrees 1,2,3; higher-moment and out-of-range configurations are not classified. Priority risk from unpublished or alternate-terminology literature.
title: Exactly \(\binom{p+r}{p}\) ordinary nodes on modular power-sum complete intersections
